subject: about observations into segments, in DSM

messages.author: 8753e7ce2213ca31
messages.subject: about observations into segments, in DSM
parts:
Hello

I have a simple question for dsm analysis (sorry if it has been previously answered, but I did not find it in the list). Once you have the segments from the transects, how to consider which observations fall into each one? I mean, do you consider the GPS position of observation on the transect line, or, do you consider the position of the observation after be 'converted' to its 'original position' with distance and azimuth?

I hope to be clear. Thanks in advance.

Natalia

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] about observations into segments, in DSM
parts:
Natalia


This is a reasonable question, perhaps rephrased as 'does the sighting belong to the segment where the observer was at time of sighting, or location of animal at time of sighting.'  I suspect others who conduct surveys have their preferred algorithm.  My suspicion is that for most instances the segment assignment is the same for both situations.  In the cases where the segment assignment would be different, the environmental conditions would be sufficiently similar in the adjacent segments that the results would not be demonstrably different.  Perhaps others have stronger views on this.

parts:
Hi Natalia,

I would concur with Eric and say that much of the time these two options
coincide. In the cases where they don't: I think you need to decide on
your rule and stick to it. I would imagine that in a great many
situations the environmental covariates in the segments are similar near
each other (for example depth or altitude are unlikely to jump up or
down from one segment to the next). I recommend documenting your
decision well so that others (including yourself the in the future) can
reproduce the steps you took in case there is some problem.

Hope this helps!
--dave
